reason: The text (Ezra 3) depicts God's restoration of Israel after exile and explicitly affirms His enduring loyalty. The people praise God saying 'For He is good, for His mercy endures forever toward Israel' (כִּ֣י ט֔וֹב כִּֽי־ לְעוֹלָ֥ם חַסְדּ֖וֹ עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל). The passage shows God facilitating the return, accepting offerings, and enabling the restoration of temple worship. There is no indication whatsoever that Yahweh considers replacing Israel with another people. The passage emphasizes covenant continuity and divine loyalty, directly contradicting the statement.
